label: Law fork under the contingent-fact PSR, applied alike to laws and adoptions
paraphrase: Premise-free consequences of the PSRStrength arena definitions. (1) For every arena, world a, fact f and selected value sel (a law, or any other content) such that f holds at a world exactly when sel there equals sel at a: if the contingent-fact PSR holds at a, then either sel is the same at every world accessible from a, or it differs at some accessible world and f has an admitted reason at a. (2) If sel is the same at every accessible world, f is not contingent at a. (3) If an operating law and a selector's adopted law coincide at every world, with facts tracking each, the contingent-fact PSR holds at a and the law differs at some accessible world, then both the law fact and the adoption fact have admitted reasons at a. (4) In a two-context model with the same finite record and the same credence the physical laws differ (3/4 and 1/4 at true), and neither gives the record zero independent-trial likelihood; the actual-law fact is contingent; with no admitted reason the contingent-fact PSR fails at the actual context, and with the everywhere-true base fact admitted as its reason the PSR holds there but that reason does not fix the law. A fact-PSR application, not the existence-PSR bridge 608a262d. It does not establish the contingent-fact PSR, that any actual law is contingent or necessary, or that an admitted reason is an intentional exercise.

connection_plan.missing_bridge: A premise that, at the actual root, the only admissible reason for a contingent law or content fact (the fork's second branch) is an intentional exercise of a rational power of that root, so that the branch yields a willed source; or a warrant that the law at the root is contingent rather than necessary (the first branch).
connection_plan.blocker: The fork is symmetric: an adopted law is a contingent fact needing its own admitted reason (clause 3), and a necessary law and a necessary adoption alike escape the contingent-fact PSR (clause 2). No premise identifies the admitted reason with intentional exercise, and an admitted reason need not fix the law (clause 4).
